Lesson 3 · Business route

Make uncertainty part of the decision

Is the average online quote meaningfully different from the matched offline quote?

The business problem

A purchasing manager is considering a rule that sends routine orders to one channel: online or local shops. The business aim is to save money without making staff spend more time searching or waiting for delivery. The team collects both quotes for the same products at the same time. That pairing matters because comparing unrelated online and shop baskets would mix a channel difference with differences in what was purchased.

What the data show

For 40 matched products, online minus offline averages 0.79 CU. The 95% interval is 0.35 to 1.22 CU.

The average online-minus-offline difference tells the manager which way the paired quotes lean. The interval describes the precision of that average; the manager’s 1.50 CU tolerance describes how large a difference would justify changing the process. Those are separate questions. Individual products also vary around the average, so a single channel rule can lose money on particular items even when the overall mean favors it. Shipping, taxes, stock, and order time belong in the final purchasing cost.

What would you decide?

Match the same product at the same time, then judge the interval against a decision-relevant cost difference. A detectable average does not mean every product is cheaper in one channel.

Use a product-level comparison for large or urgent orders and a simple convenience rule for small purchases. Record the delivered cost and the time staff spend ordering during a short pilot. At the end, judge the policy against total purchasing effort and cost, not only the quoted price gap. The manager can then decide whether a default channel helps, which products need an exception, and whether the difference is worth enforcing.

Pause and explain

Does an interval above zero prove that all online quotes are higher?

Compare your reasoning

No. It concerns the population average under the model; individual paired differences vary in both directions.

Check your judgment

Reveal the case’s known answer

The case sets the average online-minus-offline difference at 0.45 CU. The 40 matched products produce their own sample average around that value.
